Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper. Implement perf findings F1 and F15 from the analyst's report ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/report.md (read both entries; they give file:line, measurements and the fix). Branch from origin/main as `perf/streaming-output`. Files you own: crates/core/src/pipeline/rdt.rs, crates/core/src/types/interned.rs (canonical writer), and the two call sites in crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs (lines ~76 and ~82 only; another worker may edit other parts of extract.rs later, keep hunks small). Do not touch crates/semantic or core's types/semantic*.
F1: `--format rdt` with the checker builds a serde_json::Value per prop occurrence (515k occurrences, only ~3.6k distinct Arc<ParsedProp>) then to_string_pretty into one 910 MB string: 4.29 s and 3.89 GB peak on gate-large, weekly.py:115 runs exactly this. Fix: stream typed structs to a BufWriter and render each distinct Arc<ParsedProp> ONCE (cache the rendered bytes keyed by the Arc pointer: a prop sits at a fixed nesting depth in the rdt output, so the bytes match at every occurrence; verify that claim before relying on it and handle indentation correctly), splice the cached bytes, keep insertion key order (serde_json has preserve_order on here), identical escaping and spacing to serde_json's pretty printer, identical trailing newline. F15: the canonical writer serializes each distinct prop twice (interned.rs:204-211, 236-243): write the stored compact bytes as a RawValue (est. -3-6 ms; keep only if byte-identical and it gains).
Correctness is mandatory: BYTE-IDENTICAL output. Prove with `cmp` (not just JSON-equivalence) of the rdt output and the canonical output versus a build of origin/main on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src: `--format rdt` and `--format canonical`, default settings and weekly settings (`--load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`), with and without `--no-checker`; also `toon` if it shares the writer. Add tests that fail on base or guard behaviour: golden rdt fixtures with nested props, unicode/escape edge cases (quotes, control chars, U+2028), empty objects/arrays, a prop that appears at two different depths if that can occur, key order, trailing newline. Then `just test-rust`, `just test-checker-lane`, `construct:parity`. Reuse the analyst's scratch tooling in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/ (identity.sh, same.py, ab.sh); scratch in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-output/ (no /tmp). No benchmarks in parallel with other jobs: report peak RSS via `/usr/bin/time -l` and wall times from one quiet-machine A/B at the end (3 interleaved runs, medians) honestly (target: gate-large rdt 4.3 s -> well under 2 s, peak 3.9 GB -> about 1 GB). Rust 1.99.1 toolchain first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin), outside the sandbox where tests need it, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree if needed. No new scripts/options/recipes; changeset as fits (patch). Before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver`; judge by exit code. Signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`; `git push origin HEAD:perf/streaming-output` (never --no-verify; the Entire hook is fixed) and verify with `git ls-remote` that the remote SHA equals HEAD. Do not open the PR, do not poll CI. Final report <= 250 words: what changed, identity proof (cmp results per format/setting), numbers (wall, RSS), SHAs, what was not verified.

Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.

#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: identity.sh — head vs the scratch build with every experiment switched on, both fixtures, canonical JSON.
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis
mkdir -p out
for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
  case $project in
    gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
    chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
  esac
  bin/caliper-head extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > out/head-$project.json
  SYNTAX_FIX=1 TAIL_FIX=1 SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bin/caliper-phases extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > out/fix-$project.json
  SYNTAX_FIX=1 TAIL_FIX=1 SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bin/caliper-phases extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache --no-checker > out/fixnc-$project.json
  bin/caliper-head extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache --no-checker > out/headnc-$project.json
  echo "$project checker: $(python3 -I same.py out/head-$project.json out/fix-$project.json)"
  echo "$project no-checker: $(python3 -I same.py out/headnc-$project.json out/fixnc-$project.json)"
  cmp -s out/head-$project.json out/fix-$project.json && echo "$project raw bytes equal" || echo "$project raw bytes differ (stats?)"
done
#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: ab.sh <runs> <extra-args> <binary>... — interleaved extract --json --quiet --no-cache on gate-large and
# Chakra-only; wall, CPU and peak RSS from /usr/bin/time -l, one line per run. extra-args "" for none.
runs=$1; shift
extra=$1; shift
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis
for i in $(seq $runs); do
  for bin in "$@"; do
    for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
      case $project in
        gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
        chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
      esac
      out=$(/usr/bin/time -l $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache ${=extra} 2>&1 >/dev/null)
      real=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $1}')
      rss=$(echo "$out" | awk '/maximum resident/ {printf "%d", $1/1048576}')
      cpu=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $3+$5}')
      echo "$project $(basename $bin) ${real}s ${rss}MiB cpu=${cpu}s load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}')"
    done
  done
done
